t: Section 2350a(g) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by inserting after paragraph (2) the following new paragraph:“(3) The use of side-by-side testing under this subsection may be considered to be the use of competitive procedures for purposes of chapter 137 of this title, when procuring items within 5 years after an initial determination that the items have been successfully tested and found to satisfy United States military requirements or to correct operational deficiencies.”.

fable.w: This provision only deems side-by-side testing to count as competitive procedures for defense procurement purposes. A tempting reading is that "competitive procedures" or testing of items implies involvement of outside companies, but procurement and contracting are not participation in a federal decision, and no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: The use of side-by-side testing under this subsection may be considered to be the use of competitive procedures for purposes of chapter 137 of this title

opus.w: This amendment only lets the Department of Defense count side-by-side testing as using competitive procedures, so it can buy items within 5 years after they pass testing. The only outside parties that could be involved are contractors in procurement, and contract applications or bids are expressly excluded from participation. No consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue is created.
opus.s: The use of side-by-side testing under this subsection may be considered to be the use of competitive procedures for purposes of chapter 137 of this title
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that "competitive procedures" under chapter 137, the federal procurement chapter, involve outside companies, so outsiders take part. That fails the definition. Companies bidding for or supplying items are applying for contracts, which the definition expressly excludes. The amendment only lets the Department of Defense treat earlier side-by-side testing as meeting competition requirements. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside groups, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines a procurement testing method as a 'competitive procedure' for legal classification purposes. It does not require consultation with outside entities, public comment, or advisory boards. Procurement processes and contract applications are explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: The use of side-by-side testing under this subsection may be considered to be the use of competitive procedures for purposes of chapter 137 of this title, when procuring items within 5 years after an initial determination that the items have been successfully tested and found to satisfy United States military requirements or to correct operational deficiencies.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "side-by-side testing" involves contractors (outside parties) interacting with the government, thus constituting participation. However, this is a procurement process where the government is buying goods/services. The definition explicitly excludes applications for contracts. Furthermore, the text is merely defining how a specific testing method is classified for legal purposes ("considered to be the use of competitive procedures"), not establishing a new mechanism for outside consultation or advisory input into a policy decision.
